solutions.question: Prove the following trigonometric identities: (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1) = tan θ + sec θ
steps: L.H.S. = (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1)
= (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/[1 − (sec θ − tan θ)]
= (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/[1 − 1/(sec θ + tan θ)]
= (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/[(sec θ + tan θ − 1)/(sec θ + tan θ)]

solutions.question: Prove the following trigonometric identities: sin³ θ − cos³ θ = (sin θ − cos θ)(1 + sin θ cos θ)
steps: = (sin θ − cos θ)(sin² θ + sin θ cos θ + cos² θ)

solutions.answer: Hence, sin³ θ − cos³ θ = (sin θ − cos θ)(1 + sin θ cos θ).

solutions.question: Prove the following trigonometric identities: sin⁶ θ − cos⁶ θ = (sin² θ − cos² θ)(1 − sin² θ cos² θ)
steps: = (sin² θ − cos² θ)(sin⁴ θ + sin² θ cos² θ + cos⁴ θ)
= (sin² θ − cos² θ)[(sin² θ + cos² θ)² − sin² θ cos² θ]
= (sin² θ − cos² θ)(1 − sin² θ cos² θ)
solutions.answer: Hence, sin⁶ θ − cos⁶ θ = (sin² θ − cos² θ)(1 − sin² θ cos² θ).

solutions.question: From the top of a hill 300 m high, the measure of the angle of depression of a point on the nearer shore of the river is 70° and measure of the angle of depression of a point, directly across the river is 50°. steps: Let the distance from the foot of the hill to the nearer shore be BC = x m, and let the width of the river be CD = w m.
The angle of depression to the nearer shore equals the angle of elevation at C, so ∠ACB = 70°.
In right triangle ABC, tan 70° = AB / BC = 300 / x.
The angle of depression to the point directly across the river equals the angle of elevation at D, so ∠ADB = 50°.
The horizontal distance from B to D is BC + CD = x + w.
In right triangle ABD, tan 50° = AB / BD = 300 / (x + w).
solutions.answer: The width of the river is 142.5 m, and the river is 109.2 m from the foot of the hill.
